Intentionalist Intake Census

Bendini Aug 18th 2025 Version 0.5

Public census questions

Privacy policy

Your answers to the following 5 questions will be visible to anyone within the Intentionalist ecosystem. The dataset may also be made publicly available on GitHub at a later date.

Q1. Desired username

Context

Due to the small size of our ecosystem, most usernames will be available. However, because the entire point of the ecosystem is to facilitate coordination, there are rules for what kinds of usernames will be granted.[A][A]These rules have reasons behind them, but they were omitted to reduce clutter.[A]These rules have reasons behind them, but they were omitted to reduce clutter.

Username Rules
RuleDetails
Allowed charactersLatin alphabet, numbers and single hyphens only.
Length5 characters minimum, 16 maximum.
SyllablesIdeally 2 to 4.
CapitalizationFirst letter of every word, and every abbreviation of a word.
ProfessionalismDoesn’t need to be super serious, just no NSFW or political references.
AmbiguityNo usernames referring to Intentionality/Rationalist concepts, notable individuals, or ones that could be easily mistaken for another user, including common first names.
OtherA username which doesn’t technically violate the above rules, but is unsuitable for some other reason.

Q3. Nearest big city

Context

This question intends to be an elegant compromise between the need for low friction offline coordination, and people’s understandable need for online privacy. The ecosystem doesn’t need to know where you live, only where it’s convenient for you to travel to.

In order to help with this, here’s a world map of about 250 cities that should allow at least 95% of applicants to select one that’s fairly close to them.[B][B]Meaning that they were not chosen randomly, nor are they just a list of the world's 250 largest cities. They're an approximation of raw local population multiplied by their predicted Intentionality interest coefficient, then adjusted to account for distance to nearby nodes and brain drain into more prominent cities.[B]Meaning that they were not chosen randomly, nor are they just a list of the world's 250 largest cities. They're an approximation of raw local population multiplied by their predicted Intentionality interest coefficient, then adjusted to account for distance to nearby nodes and brain drain into more prominent cities.

Instructions

If you feel that the closest city to your location makes you too identifiable, pick one with a larger circle that’s slightly further away.


Give your answer as one of the following options:

Option 1 - Map reference code
Option 2 - Dropdown menu
Option 3 - Manual input

(Use this if there are no nearby cities.)

Private census questions

Privacy policy (draft)

Unlike the previous questions, your answers will be kept on a need-to-know basis unless you have consented to a specific piece of information being shared with relevant parties.

This would mean that for example if you asked for an invite to the London meetup, your email address would be shared with the London organizer, but it would not be shared with the general group of organizers, nor would it be given to an Oxford organizer so they can proactively invite you to their nearby meetup in Oxford. Despite this, it is also worth stating that although individual data will not be shared without permission, and the data will not be sent off to any third parties for analysis, it’s likely that I (Bendini) will look at this data and point out interesting patterns on internal communication channels, so long as no specific person can be identified from these observations without extensive cross-referencing.

The exact and full wording of this policy will be ironed out over time, but this is a rough approximation of how you should expect this information to be used.

Please also be aware that despite this part of the census being kept private, and most of its questions being optional, if it’s discovered that you have entered false information, it will be held against you. If you have concerns about any of these questions, please contact me and we will figure out a solution that doesn’t involve contaminating the dataset.

Tip: This webpage has been designed to work as a self-contained HTML file that can be filled out offline after the initial download, so if you wish to disconnect from the Internet to personally verify that no data is being sent back to a server, you can do so now. After you have finished the private census, you can export your answer data to a text file on your computer, and then close this webpage before reconnecting to the Internet.

Q8. Semi-precise location

Context

This question may be used to help coordiate and identify physical clusters within cities.

In the interests of maintaining some privacy while still having enough precision to be useful, if you are going to answer this question, please give your latitude and longitude rounded to 2 decimal places using Google Maps, Apple Maps, OpenStreetMap or latlong.net.

If you’re not using the mapping tool below that shows you exactly how precise 2DP coordinates are, be aware that 2DP will narrow down your location to a rectangle measuring approximately 1100m by 700m at European latitudes, meaning that someone with access to this data could identify which part of a city you live in, but not the specific street.

Q10. Preferred pronouns

Context

The purpose of this question is to accommodate reasonable requests within our ecosystem without making gender identity a bigger deal than it has to be. The idea here is for people to declare things once, and then for that information shared discreetly and automatically with all relevant parties. Doing it this way prevents the need for awkward workarounds like manually informing each new person you meet, wearing a pronoun pin, or having a group of mostly cisgender people form a circle to declare their pronouns at the start of every event.

Instructions

If you are cisgender, don’t care, or do not wish to disclose anything, please skip this question.

Inkeeping with the idea of making gender identity less salient, neopronouns like xe/zir will not be considered valid requests within the ecosystem, although you are still free to use them elsewhere without judgement. They/them is allowed as a first choice preference, but you must to specify a fallback pronoun for people who object to using the singular they in ways that are unintuitive to them.

1st choice:
2nd choice:

Q11. Other gender stuff

Context

The purpose of this question is to give individuals that are not adequately covered by the 6 pronoun combinations the opportunity to provide more context.

Unlike the previous question, this one is open to everyone, but people do need to be aware that unlike preferred pronouns, it’s not reasonable to expect most people within the ecosystem to account for any complex and bespoke relationship with gender you may have. The purpose of this box is merely to give people the opportunity to understand you better, but leaving it up to them whether they are willing and/or able to do that extra work.

Disclosure policy:

Q12. Relevant disabilities, neurodivergences or health issues

You do not have to declare anything here, but it’s hard to accommodate something unless we’re made aware of it.

A good example for a useful entry into this box would be “As a result of my ADHD I have audio processing issues which cause difficulty with remembering verbal instructions, so if you want me to do something, it should be communicated to me by text.”

Disclosure policy:

Q13. Camera preferences

Note: For practical reasons, these preferences can be superceded with an explicit declaration. For example, if an Intentionalist couple were getting married and hired a professional photographer for their wedding, the invitation could specify that by attending this event, you are automatically granting the photographer permission to take pictures that you may be present in.

Are you happy for photos and/or videos to be taken at events you’re attending?
If you have requested enhanced privacy, how do you want this request to be dealt with?
If you have requested enhanced privacy, what is your reason for doing so?
Context

You are not obligated to answer this, but a big part of our subculture 2.2.4 is that because we’re not the kind of people who enjoy following rules, when we impose a rule, we try to explain in plain language why that rule exists.

For example, here are some reasons I think most of us would perceive as legitimate:

  • “I’m Internet famous and I’m using a different username within the ecosystem to maintain privacy. While I accept that some people will inevitably recognise who I am at events, I don’t want the wider Internet to know they can find me here.”
  • “I don’t want my likeness escaping onto the public internet where it may end up as AI training data.”
  • “My line of work is politically sensitive, and while my personal beliefs pose no risk to my career, it would be unreasonable for me to demand that anyone with beliefs that are substatially different be excluded from the ecosystem just so I don’t have to explain to my boss why there’s a photo of me sitting near someone controversial at a meetup.”
  • “After seeing close friend of mine get doxxed by an Internet mob, I’ve become a lot more cautious with online privacy.”
  • “I’m early in my gender transition, and I don’t want what I look like right now to be immortalized in the ecosystem’s archives.”
Reason:
If you have given a reason, who should it be disclosed to?

Q14. Dietary requirements

Context

These 2 questions make it easier for people to get their food needs met at our events, and help those in charge of logistics plan for the complex and sometimes incompatible dietary requirements their group may have.

Hard requirements:

This box is for declaring things like a peanut allergy, celiac disease or veganism. The litmus test for inclusion is “if I hadn’t eaten in 24 hours, I would still have to refuse these food items”.


Soft requirements:

This one is for declaring things that are more like strong preferences, things like having a mild gluten sensitivity or for there to be a low carbohydrate food option. The litmus test is “I would be disappointed if it couldn’t be met, but I would probably still eat if the alternative was going hungry for 6 hours”.


Disclosure policy:

Intentionality-specific

Q15. Work and money

Context

These questions are asked partially so we can see how our ecosystem compares to the proportions found in the wider economy, and partially to get a rough idea of what could be acheived if we could e.g. coordinate 2% of the ecosystem’s total work hours towards a specific goal.

A. What is the highest level of schooling you have completed?
B. Current working arrangement
C. Industry

Other:

D. Current yearly income in USD
E. Approximate net worth in USD
Instructions

For calculation purposes, start from the Wikipedia definition[C][C]Wikipedia definition:
"For individuals, net worth or wealth refers to an individual's net economic position: the value of the individual's assets minus liabilities. Examples of assets that an individual would factor into their net worth are retirement accounts, other investments, home(s), and vehicles. Liabilities include both secured debt (such as a home mortgage) and unsecured debt (such as consumer debt or personal loans). Typically intangible assets such as educational degrees are not factored into net worth, even though such assets positively contribute to one's overall financial position."[C]Wikipedia definition:
"For individuals, net worth or wealth refers to an individual's net economic position: the value of the individual's assets minus liabilities. Examples of assets that an individual would factor into their net worth are retirement accounts, other investments, home(s), and vehicles. Liabilities include both secured debt (such as a home mortgage) and unsecured debt (such as consumer debt or personal loans). Typically intangible assets such as educational degrees are not factored into net worth, even though such assets positively contribute to one's overall financial position." and then count any home equity you have as part of your assets, but ignore the part of the mortgage that’s still outstanding.

Q17. Ecosystem-relevant skills

Instructions

Due to how many skills are listed you are not expected to give yourself ratings on all of them. If you are going to fill this question out, pick between 2 and 10 skills from this list and rate them on both proficiency and enthusiasm.

Despite what was said earlier that entering false information will be held against you, I will be very lenient on self-assessments of proficiency due to how they can vary wildly depending on who you are comparing yourself to.

On the other hand, if you rate your enthusiasm for X as a 4 or 5 and then later shirk every opportunity to do X, this will be held against you.
